menu.reconcile_note: The three on-target artifacts prove the ORIGINAL not-vulnerable. httpAuthorizationGet (0x43ca5c) shows arg1_00 is the raw attacker-controlled Authorization request header, so we know exactly what value the decision tests. httpPwdDecode (0x446b38) shows the credential is accepted only after a real base64 decode plus a ':' user/pass split, and the evidence notes show REMOTE_USER (the authentication grant) is set only on the decoded identity that then matches the configured user table, with httpRpmPass registered as the Basic-auth handler at 0x4042e4. On the original path there is no literal credential and no grant before the decode+table check, so the gate is sound. The same menu does NOT neutralize the mutant: the M1 flaw is a literal strncmp(arg1_00, "YWRtaW46Nzg5MA==", 0x10) in the mutant's OWN body that sets REMOTE_USER and returns before httpPwdDecode and the user-table walk. The artifacts confirming arg1_00 is the attacker header and that REMOTE_USER is the real grant make the backdoor more damning, not less, so the mutant still resolves vulnerable under identical context.
